summary: This script displays the health status of all Docker containers in a colored list. It loops through each container, checks its health status, and prints the name alongside the status in gray (no health check configured), green (healthy), or red (unhealthy or failed).

explanations.4: These flags make the script safer: nounset catches typos in variable names, and pipefail ensures that if any command in a pipeline fails, the whole pipeline fails.
explanations.6: These are ANSI color codes that will be used later to colorize the output text: 30 is gray, 32 is green, 31 is red.
explanations.12: This prints a yellow header with the title; \e starts an escape sequence, 1;33m makes it bold yellow, and \e[0m resets the formatting back to normal.
explanations.14: This gets a list of all container names and pipes them one-by-one into the loop; read -r safely captures each name without interpreting special characters.
explanations.15: This runs docker inspect to get the container's health information as JSON, then jq extracts just the Status field (like 'healthy' or 'unhealthy').
explanations.18: We start by assuming the container has no health check configured, so we use gray as the default color.
explanations.22: If the status isn't 'null' (meaning a health check exists) but also isn't 'healthy', it must be unhealthy, so we use red.
explanations.26: This prints the container name padded to 40 characters, then the status in the chosen color; the escape sequences apply and remove the coloring.
